transcript_text:
Meeting header: 2025-11-12 15:00 UTC | Duration 60m | Attendees: Jordan, Maya, Liam, Sophia (Redwood) + Alan, Priya, Diego (CivicStream)

Summary (auto): Co-marketing webinar planning for public sector audiences; prioritize compliance messaging and a hybrid demo+panel format. Target 200 live attendees; follow-up nurture to convert MQLs to pilot discussions.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call. We'll keep this tight, about an hour, want to come out of here with a playbook and owners.
[00:14] Alan (CivicStream): Yep, thanks Jordan. From our side Priya and Diego are on - big focus is convincing procurement and security people, so compliance notes need to be front and center.
[00:26] Maya (Redwood Marketing): totally — we were thinking the title should be explicit, like "Secure LLM Inference for Government Workloads" so it shows up in searches for public sector. Thoughts?
[00:38] Priya (CivicStream): I like explicit. Also add veteran procurement keywords, like FISMA / FedRAMP, even if we say we're not certified yet we can say readiness.
[00:50] Liam (Redwood SE): quick note — when we present specs, we should avoid exact infra promises; talk about deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated, Private (V P C / on-prem). Mention KMS/HSM and audit logs, and give an example customer flow.
[01:10] Diego (CivicStream): yes, and please use simple diagrams. Our buyers are program managers and security reviewers; they don't want deep kernel-level detail.
[01:24] Jordan: Great. On format, we suggested 30 minutes content (10-min keynote, 6-min live demo video, 14-min panel + Q&A). Live demo risks things failing — so recommend pre-recorded demo to play during session and a short live demo segment if time.
[01:41] Sophia (Redwood): I agree. Pre-recorded demo also helps with AV consistency. Liam, can you do a 6-min recorded demo showing model switch (hosted -> dedicated) and a latency/cost slide?
[01:56] Liam: Yeah I can. I'll highlight batching and KV cache improvements and show latency numbers for a 512-token sequence. Note: I might accidentally say K V cash in a sentence though, haha — I'll proof.
[02:10] Maya: also, for the landing page and registration form we need a specific field for "organization type" so we can filter for public sector leads. Jordan, can you provide required form fields?
[02:22] Jordan: We'll send recommended fields: org name, org type, role, procurement timeline, and a check box for security contact permission.
[02:30] Alan: On promotion, CivicStream can send to our partner list and a few buyers. We're expecting 50-80 signups from our channels if copy is right. What are Redwood numbers?
[02:41] Maya: We're targeting 200 registrants and 200 live attendees is optimistic, at least 150 live would be a success. We'll run a 3-email cadence plus paid LinkedIn and a small sponsored newsletter. We'll A/B subject lines and landing page CTAs.
[02:58] Priya: Important: can Redwood provide a co-branded deck and an approved security blurb we can publish? Legal will want to sign off.
[03:09] Jordan: Yes, we'll share a co-branded deck template and an "approved security statement" that Diego can review.
[03:17] Diego: Please make the statement explicit about data at rest encryption and key management; mention audit logs and optional on-prem.
[03:27] Liam: quick technical clarification we should maybe avoid saying "on-prem" as a phrase for all customers — better to say "private deployment options (V P C / on-prem)" and include a note about network isolation.
[03:40] Maya: Great. Now about speakers: proposed lineup — Jordan intro (5m), CivicStream customer story (10m) Alan or Priya, Redwood demo (pre-recorded 6m), panel with Redwood SE + CivicStream + a third-party procurement advisor (20m). Panel moderator: Sophia.
[03:58] Alan: We can do a customer story but want to keep it high-level; focus on outcomes (reduced time-to-deploy, predictable costs) rather than specific commit numbers.
[04:12] Jordan: Agreed. Also we'll include a short slide on the rollout path: pilot -> dedicated -> private. Show expected latency SLOs and how fallback routing works.
[04:22] Priya: For compliance messaging can we get a one-pager listing SOC2 / ISO roadmap and what data stays in our control? That helps our procurement folks.
[04:33] Jordan: We'll share Redwood's compliance one-pager and a note about our Private offering for customers with strict residency needs.
[04:42] Liam: On the demo content, recommend we show two short queries: one with a typical procurement prompt and one with a longer policy document ingestion to highlight memory and kv-cache behavior. I'll annotate slides about quantization and cost tradeoffs.
[04:59] Maya: Let's talk timeline: event date proposed 2025-12-11. Planning milestones: landing page draft by 11/14, email cadence by 11/18, demo video by 11/19, partner invites and co-brand deck by 11/15, tech rehearsal on 12/09. Does that timeline work?
[05:20] Priya: Yes that works from our side. We also need compliance review time; can we get the security blurb by 11/16?
[05:28] Diego: i'll review once i have the blurb. Need at least 48 hours.
[05:33] Jordan: Noted. For registration goals: target 200 registrants, 150 live, 20 SQLs within 30 days post-event. We'll pass leads to CivicStream and Redwood SDRs with tags for "public-sector-webinar".
[05:48] Sophia: Action on tracking — I'll set up UTM templates: utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term (speaker). We'll put unique parameters for CivicStream emails.
[05:58] Maya: On ads, small budget sponsored LinkedIn focusing on job titles: procurement officer, program manager, CISO. We'll test two creatives.
[06:08] Alan: On incentives — would a short invite-only follow-up roundtable with panelists help drive signups? We can offer that to procurement leads.
[06:18] Jordan: Good idea. We'll offer a "by-invite-only" follow-up workshop for qualified leads. Qualifications will be procurement timeline < 6 months and org size > 500 employees.
[06:30] Priya: Also, can Redwood provide a short technical FAQ sheet we can share pre-event? Buyers always ask about encryption and where data is processed.
[06:40] Liam: I'll draft a 1-page technical FAQ covering typical buyer Qs: KMS, key ownership, audit logs, data retention, and model governance.
[06:49] Jordan: Now, logistics: AV platform? Zoom webinar or Hopin? What's Redwood's preference?
[06:57] Maya: Zoom webinar is simplest. It integrates with our registration and can do Q&A. We'll need co-host access for CivicStream.
[07:08] Alan: fine with Zoom. We'll share list of emails that need co-host roles.
[07:15] Sophia: Rehearsal plan — two rehearsals: a content run and a tech run. Tech run to include the recorded demo playback and slide transitions. Schedule for 12/09 and a light run on 12/10.
[07:27] Jordan: Good. Any concerns about mentioning benchmarks or comparisons to other vendors?
[07:34] Diego: Avoid direct named comparisons; high-level industry references are fine.
[07:40] Maya: We'll avoid competitor slams; can include a slide on "what to evaluate" with neutral criteria.
[07:48] Alan: Audio/visual accessibility is a must for gov — please ensure captions and transcript after the event.
[07:55] Liam: We can provide auto captions and upload transcript for download. Also we'll add alt text to slides.
[08:05] Jordan: Great. Let's confirm owners quickly: Jordan (content + landing page), Maya (promotion + ads), Liam (demo + technical FAQ), Sophia (tracking + rehearsal PM), Priya (partner coordination), Diego (security sign-off).
[08:21] Priya: Confirmed.
[08:24] Maya: One more thing — what is the call-to-action? Is it "request pilot" or "book a security consult"? We should A/B test.
[08:33] Jordan: I vote main CTA: "Book a pilot conversation" and secondary CTA: "Request security consult". We'll test which converts better.
[08:41] Alan: That works.
[08:44] Jordan: Okay, recap and next steps — I'll send the draft landing page and speaker bios by 11/14. Maya will share the email cadence and ad mocks by 11/18. Liam will deliver demo video by 11/19. We'll reconvene next week for a short check-in on assets.
[08:59] Priya: Thanks all.
[09:02] Jordan: Thanks folks, meeting adjourned.
